questions.question: How does a workflow template reference a lifecycle state?
options: Through a dropdown that lists all available lifecycle states
By the Set State robot activity, which references the state name as text
Through an automatic link created when the workflow is attached to a lifecycle
By the lifecycle template ID embedded in the workflow XML
questions.rationale: The Set State robot activity in the workflow references a lifecycle state by name as a text string. There is no dropdown validation or automatic cross-checking. If the state name doesn't match, the error occurs at runtime, not at configuration time.

questions.question: When does a state name mismatch between a workflow and lifecycle template produce an error?
options: When the workflow template is saved
When the lifecycle template is saved
At runtime when the workflow tries to execute the Set State activity
During the nightly system validation job
questions.rationale: State name mismatches cause runtime errors, not build-time errors. If you restructure a lifecycle without updating associated workflows, the failure only surfaces when a user triggers the transition and the workflow attempts to execute the Set State activity.

questions.question: What is the primary gap in Windchill's OIR table for finding rules by type?
options: The table does not support any search functionality
Rules are sorted randomly and cannot be reordered
Soft type identifiers use internal branch ID format instead of readable names
OIR rules can only be viewed by system administrators
questions.rationale: The OIR table has text search but no filter-by-type function. For soft types, the type identifier uses an internal branch ID format (e.g., wt.doc.WTDocument|8666) rather than a readable name. A community-built QML report can map these IDs to readable names, but no OOTB solution exists.

questions.question: In the configuration chain (OIR → Lifecycle → Workflow), what is the most important characteristic of failure modes?
options: Failures are caught at configuration time by validation checks
Failures always produce clear error messages identifying the broken link
Failures in any link surface at runtime, not at configuration time
Failures cascade automatically — one broken link disables the entire chain
questions.rationale: Failures in the OIR → Lifecycle → Workflow chain surface at runtime, not at configuration time. There is no cross-validation between the three configuration surfaces. This makes chain-tracing from object creation the most efficient debugging approach.
